mainTopic: Why each opinion learns the blind person's exclusion from a different source, and the details of סמיכה: who leans, where, with what, and how it compares to תנופה
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of why one opinion learns from עולת ראיה and the other from the זקני העדה that a blind person does not do סמיכה. Then the גמרא goes through the משנה's rules of סמיכה one by one. Three times the תורה says ״יָדוֹ״, and these exclude a slave, an agent and a wife from leaning for the owner. סמיכה is a שיירי מצוה: skipping it counts against the owner, but the קרבן still atones, and the same is true of תנופה. Hands go on the head, not on the neck, back, breast or sides, and nothing may come between the hands and the animal. ריש לקיש learns that two hands are needed, and the גמרא tells the story of רבי אלעזר repeating that teaching without credit. That story ends with the rule narrowed to סמיכה on an animal. After explaining that the שחיטה is done right where the סמיכה happened, a new משנה begins comparing the strict points of סמיכה and תנופה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Learn an individual's offering from an individual's offering
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that learns from עולת ראיה does not learn from the זקני העדה, because an individual's קרבן is learned from another individual's קרבן, not from a communal one.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn an individual's offering from another individual's offering. We do not learn an individual's offering from a communal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it asked just before this section: why doesn't the opinion that learns from עולת ראיה learn from the זקני העדה instead?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular סמיכה is done by one person on his own קרבן. עולת ראיה is also one person's offering, so it is the closer comparison. The bull of the זקני העדה is a קרבן ציבור (communal offering), so this opinion holds it is too different to learn from.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive / compare and learn one law from another

phrases.english: We derive an individual from an individual,
phrases.notes: He means: an individual's קרבן from another individual's קרבן, like עולת ראיה.

phrases.english: but we do not derive an individual from the community.
phrases.notes: The communal offering here is the bull that the זקני העדה lean on.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין יָחִיד מִיָּחִיד, וְאֵין דָּנִין יָחִיד מִצִּיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question that came right before this section, about the opinion that learns from עולת ראיה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the opinion that learns from עולת ראיה does not learn from the זקני העדה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An individual's קרבן should be learned from another individual's קרבן, not from a communal קרבן.

steps.title: Why doesn't the other opinion learn from עולת ראיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the question and asks why the opinion that learns from the זקני העדה does not learn from עולת ראיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who learns from the elders of the congregation, why doesn't he learn from the burnt offering of appearance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the reverse question, and the next step will give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that עולת ראיה looks like the better comparison, since both are individual offerings. So the opinion that chose the communal bull of the זקני העדה needs a reason why he skipped עולת ראיה.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders of the congregation, who lean their hands on the communal bull (ויקרא 4:15)
The burnt offering brought when a person comes to the בית המקדש on the festivals

phrases.english: And according to the one who derives it from the elders of the congregation,
phrases.notes: "It" is the rule that a blind person does not do סמיכה.

phrases.english: what is the reason he does not derive it
from the burnt offering of appearance?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּיָלֵיף מִזִּקְנֵי עֵדָה, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא יָלֵיף מֵעוֹלַת רְאִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of the question answered in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the opinion that learns from the זקני העדה rejects learning from עולת ראיה.

steps.title: Learn from a case where סמיכה is written explicitly
steps.stepSummary: We learn from a case where the תורה writes סמיכה directly. עולת ראיה does not have סמיכה written about it; its own סמיכה is learned from עולת נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn something that has סמיכה written about it directly from something else that has סמיכה written about it directly. That leaves out עולת ראיה, because its own סמיכה is learned from a voluntary burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why this opinion prefers the זקני העדה. The תורה writes סמיכה explicitly about the communal bull, but not about עולת ראיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion cares more about where סמיכה is actually written than about whether the offering is individual or communal. The general סמיכה פסוק and the זקני העדה פסוק both say סמיכה outright. עולת ראיה only has סמיכה because it is learned from עולת נדבה, so it is a weaker source.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the קרבן
About that case itself, written directly

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two different ways to pick the best source: how alike the two cases are (individual vs. communal), or how direct the source is (written explicitly vs. itself learned from somewhere else).

phrases.aramaic: דָּנִין מִידֵּי דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ סְמִיכָה בְּגוּפֵיהּ,
phrases.english: We derive a matter about which סמיכה is written in its own right,
from a matter about which סמיכה is written in its own right,
phrases.notes: This is the bull of the זקני העדה.

phrases.english: to exclude the burnt offering of appearance,
since it itself is learned from a voluntary burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין מִידֵּי דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ סְמִיכָה בְּגוּפֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We learn only from a source where סמיכה is written explicitly. עולת ראיה's סמיכה is itself learned from עולת נדבה, so it is excluded.

steps.title: Source that עולת חובה learns סמיכה from עולת נדבה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ in the פסוק about אהרן's offering as "like the law of a voluntary burnt offering", which teaches that an obligatory burnt offering needs סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב יצחק בר אבא: "And he brought the burnt offering and did it according to the law" means according to the law of a voluntary burnt offering. This teaches that an obligatory burnt offering requires סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim from step 3 that עולת ראיה's סמיכה is only learned from עולת נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה writes סמיכה about voluntary burnt offerings. The word ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ stretches that law to every obligatory burnt offering, and עולת ראיה is one of them. So עולת ראיה has סמיכה only through this extra step.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the law (here: the law of עולת נדבה)

steps.whatToRemember: The opinion that learns from the זקני העדה prefers a source where סמיכה is written outright. The opinion that learns from עולת ראיה prefers an individual's קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: As a tanna taught before Rav Yitzchak bar Abba:
"And he presented the burnt offering
phrases.notes: ויקרא 9:16, about אהרן's offering on the eighth day of the inauguration.

phrases.english: and did it according to the law" —
according to the law of a voluntary burnt offering,
this teaches about an obligatory burnt offering
that it requires סמיכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim at the end of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That עולת ראיה's requirement of סמיכה is learned from עולת נדבה, not written directly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught before רב יצחק בר אבא, reading ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ in ויקרא 9:16.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: slave, agent and woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, which lists the עבד, the שליח and the אשה among those who do not do סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the slave, and the agent, and the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new piece of the משנה. This line sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these three people do not lean hands on a קרבן. The גמרא now wants to show where in the תורה this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent who brings the קרבן for the owner

phrases.english: And the slave, and the agent, and the woman.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, which lists people who don't do סמיכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the blind person discussion and starts the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave, an agent and a woman do not do סמיכה.

steps.title: ״יָדוֹ״ three times excludes slave, agent and wife
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the three times the תורה says ״יָדוֹ״ (his hand) that the owner's slave, agent and wife cannot do סמיכה for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "His hand", and not his slave's hand. "His hand", and not his agent's hand. "His hand", and not his wife's hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the משנה's rule about the slave, the agent and the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says ״יָדוֹ״ three times in the chapter about סמיכה. Each time is read as "only the owner's own hand". Each one leaves out a different person who might have leaned for the owner: his slave, his agent, or his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: His hand — the owner's own hand

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about the owner's own קרבן. It teaches that someone else cannot lean in his place. It is not discussing the slave's or the woman's own קרבנות.
steps.whatToRemember: סמיכה must be done personally by the owner's own hand. A slave, an agent or a wife cannot do it for him.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"His hand" — and not the hand of his slave,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:2

phrases.english: "His hand" — and not the hand of his agent,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:8

phrases.english: "His hand" — and not the hand of his wife.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That a slave, an agent and a wife cannot do סמיכה on the owner's קרבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the three times ״יָדוֹ״ appears in ויקרא chapter 3.

steps.title: Why do we need all three exclusions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה needed three separate ״ידו״ words to exclude the עבד, the שליח and the אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תורה needed three separate words to teach us about three people. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא will explain that each one is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the תורה does not waste words. If one ״ידו״ could exclude everyone except the owner, the other two would be extra. So the גמרא asks what each one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question asking why something extra was written

phrases.english: Why do I need all these?
phrases.notes: He means the three times ״ידו״ appears, from the ברייתא in the step before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the three-fold derivation from ״ידו״ given in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three mentions of ״ידו״ adds that the others could not teach.

steps.title: Each exclusion is needed: slave, agent and wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that each case has its own reason why we might have allowed it, so all three exclusions are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If the תורה had written only one, I would have said it excludes the slave, because he is not obligated in מצוות. But an agent is obligated in מצוות, and a person's agent is like himself, so I would say he may do סמיכה. And if the תורה had taught only these two, I would say they are excluded because they are not like the owner's own body. But a wife is like his own body, so I would say she may do סמיכה. So all three are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a צריכא: each person is a 'stronger' case than the one before, so each needs its own exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד is the easiest to exclude because he is not a full בר מצוות. A שליח is a full בר מצוות, and we have the rule שלוחו של אדם כמותו, so we might think he can stand in for the owner. A wife is treated like her husband's own body, so we would think she is even closer than a שליח. That is why the תורה had to exclude her separately.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. Each source teaches something the others could not
I would have thought. The mistaken idea we might have had
A person's agent counts like the person himself

steps.whatToRemember: The order goes from weakest to strongest: an עבד is not a full בר מצוות, a שליח counts like the owner, and a wife is like his own body. Even so, none of them can do סמיכה for the owner.

phrases.english: It is necessary.
If the Merciful One had written only one,
I would have said it is to exclude a slave,
since he is not obligated in מצוות,
phrases.notes: A Canaanite slave keeps only some of the מצוות, so he is not a full בר מצוות.

phrases.english: but an agent, who is obligated in מצוות,
and a person's agent is like himself,
I would say he may place hands.
And if it had taught us only these two,
since they are not like his own body,
but his wife, who is like his own body,
I would say she may place hands.
So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each exclusion is needed because the שליח and the אשה each have a reason, stronger than the one before, why we might have allowed them to do סמיכה.

steps.title: The משנה: סמיכה is a non-essential part of the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: סמיכה is a שיירי מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Placing hands is a non-essential part of the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on and quotes the next words of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that will explain what these words mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling סמיכה a שיירי מצוה means the קרבן still works even if the owner did not do סמיכה. It is part of the מצוה, but the קרבן does not depend on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'leftovers' of a מצוה. A part that should be done but does not hold back the main result

steps.confusionAlert: שיירי מצוה does not mean it is optional. You are still supposed to do סמיכה. It only means that skipping it does not stop the קרבן from working.

phrases.english: Placing hands is a non-essential part of the מצוה.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the leftovers of a מצוה', meaning a part that does not hold back the קרבן from working.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה, after finishing the topic of who does סמיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סמיכה is a שיירי מצוה; it does not hold back the קרבן.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains how סמיכה relates to atonement
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how ״וסמך... ונרצה״ can link סמיכה to atonement when only the blood atones. It answers that skipping סמיכה counts as if there was no atonement, but there really is atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: ״And he shall place his hand... and it shall be accepted.״ Does placing hands bring atonement? Isn't atonement only through the blood, as it says, ״For the blood atones through the soul״? Rather, it comes to tell you: if he treated סמיכה as a non-essential part of the מצוה, the פסוק considers it as if he did not get atonement, but he did get atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports and explains the משנה's statement that סמיכה is a שיירי מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts סמיכה right next to ״ונרצה״, which sounds like סמיכה brings atonement. But another פסוק says only the blood atones. So the ברייתא explains: skipping סמיכה is counted against him as if he had no atonement, yet in fact the קרבן did atone. That is exactly what שיירי מצוה means.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall be accepted, meaning the קרבן is accepted to bring atonement
The פסוק considers it against him as if...

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that something can be fully part of a מצוה and still not hold it back. The person loses something by skipping it, but the קרבן is still valid.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And he shall place his hand" ... "and it shall be accepted"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:4

phrases.english: But does placing hands bring atonement?
Isn't atonement only through the blood,
as it is said: "For it is the blood that atones through the soul"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:11

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you
that if he treated placing hands as a non-essential part of the מצוה,
phrases.notes: He means he skipped it, thinking it doesn't really matter.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ לֹא כִּיפֵּר,
phrases.english: the verse considers it against him as if he did not get atonement,
but he did get atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to explain and support the משנה's phrase in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That סמיכה is a שיירי מצוה: important, but it does not hold back atonement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 1:4 together with ויקרא 17:11.

steps.title: The same rule is taught about תנופה
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא makes the same point about waving (תנופה): skipping it counts as if there was no atonement, but there really is atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught about waving in the same way: ״to be waved to atone.״ Does waving bring atonement? Isn't atonement only through the blood, as it says, ״For the blood atones through the soul״? Rather, it comes to tell you: if he treated waving as a non-essential part of the מצוה, the פסוק considers it as if he did not get atonement, but he did get atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא showing that תנופה follows the same rule as סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the פסוק links תנופה to atonement with ״לכפר״, even though only the blood atones. The ברייתא answers the same way: skipping תנופה is counted against him, but the קרבן still atones. This shows the idea is a general pattern and not something special to סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving parts of a קרבן back and forth before ה׳
In the same way, like this

steps.whatToRemember: סמיכה and תנופה are both שיירי מצוה. Only the blood brings atonement. Skipping these parts is counted against the person, but the קרבן still atones.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא גַּבֵּי תְנוּפָה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא:
phrases.english: And it was taught about waving in the same way:
"to be waved, to atone"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:21

phrases.english: But does waving bring atonement?
Isn't atonement only through the blood,
as it is said: "For it is the blood that atones through the soul"!
Rather, it comes to tell you
that if he treated waving as a non-essential part of the מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ לֹא כִּיפֵּר,
phrases.english: the verse considers it against him as if he did not get atonement,
but he did get atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא גַּבֵּי תְנוּפָה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא with the same structure, applied to תנופה.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'as if he did not atone, but he did atone' reading is a general pattern for שיירי מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 14:21 about the אשם of the מצורע.

steps.title: Hands must be placed on the head, not the neck, back or breast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'on the head.' A ברייתא uses three repeated פסוקים to exclude the neck, the back and the breast.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On the head.' The Sages taught: 'His hand upon the head,' and not on the neck. 'His hand upon the head,' and not on the back. 'His hand upon the head,' and not on the breast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, 'on the head.' It brings a ברייתא showing that סמיכה must be done on the head and nowhere else on the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'his hand upon the head' appears three times in the section on שלמים. The ברייתא reads each time as ruling out a different body part: the neck, the back and the breast.

phrases.english: "On the head,"
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״יָדוֹ עַל הָרֹאשׁ״ – וְלֹא יָדוֹ עַל הַצַּוָּאר,
phrases.english: "His hand upon the head" (and not his hand on the neck);
phrases.notes: This phrase shows up three times in ויקרא פרק ג (3:2, 3:8, 3:13). Each time it rules out one more spot.

phrases.aramaic: ״יָדוֹ עַל הָרֹאשׁ״ – וְלֹא יָדוֹ עַל הַגַּבַּיִים,
phrases.english: "His hand upon the head" (and not his hand on the back);

phrases.aramaic: ״יָדוֹ עַל הָרֹאשׁ״ – וְלֹא יָדוֹ עַל הֶחָזֶה.
phrases.english: "His hand upon the head" (and not his hand on the breast).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the משנה after finishing the discussion of סמיכה as שיירי מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סמיכה must be done on the head; the neck, back and breast are each excluded by a separate פסוק.

steps.title: Why are three exclusions needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה needed three separate phrases to exclude three body parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why three exclusions are needed. If the head is required, one phrase should be enough to rule out everything else. This sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that one 'on the head' would already teach 'only the head.' So the other two phrases look extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need all these? A question about seemingly extra wording

phrases.english: Why do I need all these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the three repeated phrases in the ברייתא of step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תורה repeats 'his hand upon the head' three times.

steps.title: The back needs its own exclusion
steps.stepSummary: With only one exclusion, we would rule out the neck, which is lower than the head. We might still allow the back, which is level with the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all needed. If the Merciful One wrote only one, to exclude the neck, that would be because the neck is not level with the head. But the back, which is level with the head, I would say is allowed. So a second one is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering. It shows why we need a separate exclusion for the back, beyond the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neck hangs lower than the head, so it is easy to rule out. The back is level with the head, so we might think it is close enough. A second פסוק teaches that the back is also ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. Each source teaches something new
I would say; what we might have thought

phrases.english: They are necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written only one
to exclude the neck,
because it does not stand level with its head,
but its back, which stands level with its head,
I would say it is not excluded,
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13, first part.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The back is level with the head, so we might have allowed it. A second exclusion is needed.

steps.title: The breast needs its own exclusion
steps.stepSummary: With only two exclusions, we might allow the breast, since the breast is part of the תנופה (waving), unlike the neck and back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it taught only these two, that would be because they are not part of the waving. But the breast, which is part of the waving, I would say is allowed. So a third one is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows why the breast needs a third exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neck and back are not waved, so they are less important. The חזה of a שלמים is waved in the תנופה, so we might think it is important enough for סמיכה. The third פסוק rules that out too.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving of parts of the offering

steps.whatToRemember: סמיכה must be on the head. Three פסוקים rule out the neck (lower than the head), the back (level with the head) and the breast (part of the waving).

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only these two,
that would be because they are not included in the waving,
but the breast, which is included in the waving,
I would say it is not excluded; so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The breast is part of the תנופה, so we might have allowed it. A third exclusion is needed.

steps.title: What about the sides of the head?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages asked whether placing a hand on the sides of the animal's head counts as סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if his hand is on the sides, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised. Does it count if someone puts his hand on the side of the head instead of the top? The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sides are part of the head, so they might count as 'on the head.' Or perhaps the top of the head is required.

keyTerms.meaning: An open question raised in the בית מדרש

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If his hand is on the sides, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the sides of the animal's head, not its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: יָדוֹ עַל הַצְּדָדִין, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a further case beyond the three parts excluded in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether סמיכה on the sides of the head is valid.

steps.title: The sides of the head do not count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from אבא בירא son of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads 'his hand upon its head' as excluding the sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: אבא בירא son of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: 'His hand upon its head,' and not his hand on the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from a ברייתא. Placing the hand on the sides does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק as requiring the hand on the head itself, meaning its top. The sides are ruled out, so the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: On its head; read here as on top of the head

steps.whatToRemember: סמיכה must be on top of the animal's head. The sides of the head do not count.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא בִּירָאָה בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Abba Bira'a, son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, says:
"His hand upon its head" (means on top of its head),
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:4

phrases.english: and not his hand on the sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא בִּירָאָה בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That סמיכה on the sides of the head is invalid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of אבא בירא son of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reading 'his hand upon its head' (ויקרא 1:4).

steps.title: Does a cloth on the hands block the leaning?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether a cloth between the hands and the animal counts as a barrier for סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if there is a cloth on the hands, does it count as something in between?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question about סמיכה. If a cloth sits between a person's hands and the animal, is the סמיכה still valid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with where on the animal the hands go. Now the question is about the hands themselves. Must there be direct contact, or is a thin cloth acceptable?

keyTerms.meaning: Something in between that blocks contact (a barrier)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
A cloth: does it count as a barrier?
phrases.notes: He means a cloth wrapped on the hands, sitting between the hands and the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the hands go to what may come between the hands and the animal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a cloth invalidates סמיכה as a barrier.

steps.title: Nothing may come between him and the offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that nothing may come between the person and the קרבן, so a cloth does block.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: as long as nothing comes between him and the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי ירמיה with a ברייתא. סמיכה is valid only when nothing comes between the person and the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a general rule: no barrier at all. A cloth is a barrier, so it would make the סמיכה invalid. The question is answered directly from an earlier source.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
provided that there is no item interposing
between him and the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the cloth.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Any barrier, including a cloth, invalidates סמיכה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that two hands are needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that סמיכה is done with two hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that it is done with two hands: where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another detail in the משנה: סמיכה must be done with both hands. It asks for the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual פסוקים about סמיכה say "his hand" in the singular. So the גמרא needs to explain where two hands come from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters learned? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And with two hands:
from where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for using two hands.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: "his hand" means two unless the פסוק says one
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns from אהרן's סמיכה that wherever the תורה says "his hand," it means two hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says "אהרן shall place both his hands." The word is spelled like "his hand," but it also says "both." This sets a pattern: wherever it says "his hand," it means two, unless the פסוק says "one."
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the source. A פסוק writes the word for "hand" in a singular-looking spelling but adds "both." That pattern tells us "his hand" normally means two hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about אהרן, the word ידו is spelled like the singular, yet the word "both" shows it means two. ריש לקיש turns this into a general rule, a בנין אב. Every "his hand" means two hands, unless the תורה says "one."

keyTerms.meaning: Built a paradigm, a model case that teaches a general rule
It is written (the spelling in the text)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shapes how we read every "his hand" in the תורה, and it is what the rest of this section argues about.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: as the verse says
"And Aaron shall place both his hands"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:21

phrases.english: it is written "his hand," and it is written "both."
phrases.notes: The word is spelled without the second yod, so on its own it looks like "his hand."

phrases.english: This established a paradigm:
any place where it says "his hand,"
there are two here,
unless the verse specifies to you "one."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the source for two hands.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בנין אב from ויקרא 16:21: "his hand" always means two unless "one" is specified.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר repeats the teaching without credit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says ריש לקיש's teaching in the בית מדרש without naming him, and ריש לקיש is upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר went and said this teaching in the study hall, but did not say it in ריש לקיש's name. ריש לקיש heard and became angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי אלעזר repeated ריש לקיש's teaching without saying whose it was, and ריש לקיש got angry. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story explains what happens next: ריש לקיש is upset and responds sharply. Saying a teaching without naming its author is the reason given for his anger.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar went
and said this teaching in the study hall,
but did not say it in the name of Reish Lakish.
Reish Lakish heard and became angry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about how the teaching from step 21 was passed on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: the teaching was repeated without credit, angering ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Why would the תורה ever write "his hands"?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי אלעזר: if "his hand" already means two, why does the תורה also write "his hands"?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: if you think that wherever it says "his hand" it means two, why does the תורה need to write "his hands" over and over?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks the very rule that רבי אלעזר just taught. If "his hand" already means two, the plural "his hands" would be unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is that the תורה does not waste words. If the singular already means two, then the many plural spellings ידיו would add nothing. So the rule seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you really think so)
Why do I need it? (asking what is extra)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule being attacked is ריש לקיש's own rule, but he is challenging it as רבי אלעזר said it, right after the story of his anger.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it enters your mind
that wherever "his hand" is written, they are two,
why do I need it to write "his hands," "his hands"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story, ריש לקיש challenges the teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בנין אב that "his hand" always means two.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the singular already means two, the plural spellings would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Twenty-four examples of "his hands," and רבי אלעזר is silent
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש backs up his challenge with twenty-four פסוקים that use ידיו, and רבי אלעזר has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him with twenty-four places that say "his hands," such as "His hands shall bring," "his hands shall contend for him," and "guiding his hands." רבי אלעזר was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש lists twenty-four places where the תורה writes "his hands" in the plural. רבי אלעזר cannot answer and stays quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The examples show the challenge is not about one odd פסוק. The plural appears many times, which makes the question much stronger. רבי אלעזר has no reply, but the next step gives the answer he could have given.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש learns two hands from "both his hands" (ויקרא 16:21). רבי אלעזר repeats the rule without credit. ריש לקיש then challenges it with twenty-four plural ידיו, and רבי אלעזר stays silent. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: He challenged him with twenty-four "his hands":
"His hands shall bring,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:30

phrases.english: "his hands shall contend for him,"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7

phrases.english: "guiding his hands wittingly."
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:14

phrases.english: He was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge from step 23 with examples, and ends with silence.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that "his hand" means two.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Twenty-four plural spellings would all be unnecessary if the singular already meant two.

steps.title: ריש לקיש supplies the answer רבי אלעזר could have given
steps.stepSummary: Once he calms down, ריש לקיש tells רבי אלעזר he could have answered that the rule 'his hand means two hands' was said only about סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he calmed down, ריש לקיש said to רבי אלעזר: Why didn't you answer me that I was only talking about 'his hands' in the case of סמיכה?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש himself gives the answer to his own challenge, the one רבי אלעזר could not answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge asked why the תורה ever needs to write ידיו if ידו already means two hands. The answer: the rule that ידו means two hands applies only to סמיכה. Everywhere else ידו means one hand, so the תורה must write ידיו when it means two.

keyTerms.meaning: his mind calmed down; he was no longer upset

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not dropping his own rule. He is narrowing it, saying it was only ever meant for סמיכה.

phrases.english: After his mind had calmed down,
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש, who was upset with רבי אלעזר in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: he said to him:
Why did you not say to me,
"I was talking about 'his hands' of leaning (סמיכה)"?
phrases.notes: He means the rule 'his hand means two hands' is only for סמיכה. Anywhere else, two hands needs the word ידיו.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר דְּנָח דַּעְתֵּיהּ אֲמַר לֵיהּ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תֵּימָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 23 and 24 that רבי אלעזר could not answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule 'his hand means two hands' applies everywhere in the תורה, so ידיו would never be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only to סמיכה. In other places, ידיו is needed to mean two hands.

steps.title: But a פסוק about leaning also says his hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even with סמיכה the תורה writes ידיו, about משה leaning on יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with סמיכה too it is written: 'And he leaned his hands upon him and commanded him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by showing a פסוק about סמיכה that still uses the word ידיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ידו means two hands whenever the topic is סמיכה, the תורה should not need ידיו for סמיכה at all. Yet when משה leaned on יהושע, the פסוק says ידיו. So 'only for סמיכה' seems too broad.

phrases.english: With leaning (סמיכה), too, it is written:
"And he leaned his hands upon him and commanded him"
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:23. משה is leaning his hands on יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the rule ידו means two hands applies to all סמיכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק about סמיכה (משה and יהושע) still uses ידיו, so the plural is needed even for סמיכה.

steps.title: The rule was only about leaning on an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the answer further: the rule is only about סמיכה on an animal offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: I was talking about leaning on an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer so that ריש לקיש's rule covers only leaning hands on a קרבן animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה leaning on יהושע is not leaning on an animal, so it falls outside the rule, and the תורה needed ידיו there. For a קרבן, ידו still means two hands.

keyTerms.meaning: I was saying, I was talking about

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's rule is that ידו means two hands only for סמיכה on an animal קרבן. Everywhere else, the תורה writes ידיו for two hands.

phrases.english: I was talking about leaning on an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by narrowing the rule even more.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers every kind of סמיכה, including leaning on a person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only סמיכה on an animal offering.

steps.title: What does the משנה mean about the place and the timing of slaughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about where and when the שחיטה is done and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'In the place where they lean, they slaughter; right after leaning comes slaughter.' What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the words of the משנה and asks how to read this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It looks like two separate rules: one about place and one about timing. But if the slaughter comes right after the leaning, it obviously happens in the same place. So why would the משנה need to say both?

keyTerms.meaning: what is it saying? (asking how to read the words)

phrases.english: And in the place where they lean, they slaughter,
right after leaning comes slaughter.
What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ריש לקיש story and goes back to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה is giving two separate rules or one, since one part seems to make the other unnecessary.

steps.title: It is one rule with its reason
steps.stepSummary: The second half explains the first: they slaughter in the same place because the שחיטה must come right after the סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: in the place where they lean, they slaughter, because right after leaning comes slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the line as one rule followed by its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reading the words as 'because right after leaning comes slaughter,' the timing part becomes the reason for the place part. Nothing in the משנה is extra anymore.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means (rereading the words)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
In the place where they lean, they slaughter,
because right after leaning comes slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second clause is the reason for the first: same place, because the slaughter must come right away.

steps.title: New mishna: each of leaning and waving is stricter in some way
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says סמיכה and תנופה are each stricter than the other in some way, and gives the first difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Leaning is stricter than waving in one way, and waving is stricter than leaning in another way. One partner may wave for all the partners, but one partner may not lean for all the partners.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It compares סמיכה with תנופה and first shows how סמיכה is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When several partners bring one קרבן, one of them can do the תנופה for everyone. סמיכה is different: each partner must lean his own hands, so in this way סמיכה is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: partners who bring a קרבן together

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There is a stricter point in leaning than in waving,
and in waving than in leaning.
For one person waves for all the partners,
but one person does not lean for all the partners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One partner may wave for all the partners, but each partner must lean for himself.

steps.title: How waving is stricter: it applies to both individual and communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins the stricter point of תנופה: it is done with both private and communal קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stricter point in waving: waving is done with the קרבנות of an individual and with the קרבנות of the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the other side and starts showing how תנופה is stricter than סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנופה is done both for a single person's קרבן and for the whole community's קרבן, so it applies in more cases. The משנה keeps going past this point to finish the contrast with סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: offerings brought for the whole community

phrases.english: The stricter point in waving:
that waving is done
with offerings of an individual and with offerings of the community,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the comparison started in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנופה applies to both individual and communal קרבנות.
